draft.title: Plate tectonics
card: The lithosphere is Earth's rigid outer layer, made of the crust and the top of the mantle. It is broken into large pieces called plates.
The plates move slowly, by a few centimetres a year. They float on the softer, hotter rock below.
two plates move towards each other. This can build mountain ranges, cause earthquakes, and form volcanoes where one plate sinks under another.
two plates move apart. Magma can rise to fill the gap, and earthquakes and volcanoes can occur there too.
draft.remember: Slow plate movement at the edges of plates causes earthquakes, volcanoes and mountain building.

opts: Rigid outer layer of Earth, broken into moving plates
Layer of molten rock that lies beneath the crust
Single solid shell that does not move at all
Layer of gases that surrounds the Earth
a.why: The lithosphere is the rigid crust and top of the mantle, and it is broken into plates. The softer rock below it is not the lithosphere, and the plates do move, though slowly.
a.clue: Think of the hard outer shell that is cracked into pieces.

b.q: Two plates in a mountain region are slowly moving towards each other. Which boundary is this, and what can it cause?
opts: Convergent, which can build mountains and cause earthquakes
Divergent, which can build mountains and cause earthquakes
Convergent, which can pull the crust apart into a gap
Divergent, which can push the plates together and fold them
b.why: Plates moving towards each other form a convergent boundary, where pushing can build mountains and cause earthquakes. Divergent boundaries are where plates move apart, so they do not fit this case.
b.clue: Look at the direction the plates are moving, towards or apart.

a.best: Rigid outer layer of Earth, broken into moving plates

b.best: Convergent, which can build mountains and cause earthquakes
